substeps.caption: Each tray that needs services carries a coupling at its back right corner; a dock in the column's side wall meets it in the slot, and another in the bay. The parts are Staubli's CombiTac: two frames, the electrical one above the fluid one, as Staubli requires. The fluid frame ends in a vacuum line, for the trays that use one and always in the bay.
The tray's face (the dock and the wall hidden for the view).

On the tray, the socket halves: power, its earth and a monitoring pair; Ethernet; air, nitrogen, chilled water in and out, and vacuum. The sockets are touch-safe and every face is flat, so nothing stands proud of the tray's side.
On the dock, the pin halves, on a plate that floats on four springs. The pins' lengths set the order things connect: PE first, the LMFB pair last.

The gearmotor turns the crank and the head comes in. This tray stopped 2.5 mm off in y and 1.5 mm low: the align 4 pins find their cones and the plate, floating on four springs, follows them (align 4 takes up 4 mm).
The last 15 mm, at Staubli's mating speed (10 mm/s, shown 3 times slower): first the electrical frame, from above, its carriers drawn see-through.
PE makes first, then Ethernet and L1/L2/N; the LMFB pair makes last, so it only closes once everything else is home. The hard-stop screws take the end force, not the contacts.
The same 15 mm again, for the fluid frame below, its bodies see-through.

Each plug's nose pushes the socket's sleeve back while the socket's piston pushes the plug's poppet back: the flow opens only once both seals are inside each other, and shuts again the same way. The vacuum pair has no valves: its nose seals in an O-ring with 3.5 mm to go.

Only with the LMFB loop closed does the dock's relay let the contactor close, so the contacts never mate or part under load; then the valves open, the vacuum's isolation valve last. The crank stops at dead centre: the couplings' 175 N of springs can't push the head back, powered or not.

Vacuum, on trays B, K and M and always in the bay: Staubli's largest bore, an open-flow UCT08 pair, between two normally closed valves. A scroll pump on the floor keeps the riser at its base pressure, where it runs quiet; each tray only pumps its own few litres. Staubli rates the pair to 14 mbar: lower needs its confirmation.

To let go, in reverse: the contactor opens first (the tray's UPS takes over), then the valves shut and vent each coupling's side of the line, and the sensors confirm 0 bar. For vacuum the tray's valve and the isolation valve shut and N2 fills the stretch between them to atmospheric: no coupling parts with pressure across it.
The head pulls back 75 mm: the LMFB pair breaks first, PE last, and each coupling's valves shut flush before its faces part. The align pins' tips end 18.8 mm clear of the tray's side.
The extractor takes the tray: nothing on it stands proud of its side, and its sockets are touch-safe (IP2X). In transit its UPS carries it, until the bay's dock does all this again.
